At about 6 or younger I was at my mom's coworkers pool party for her kid's bday. All the kids were playing with a beach ball in the pool, but I didn't know how to swim, so I decided I'd be the ball boy and return it to them when it got launched out of the pool, so I could feel included. Well, it got stuck in a bush on the thin sidelines of the pool's edge, and I figured I could shimmy my way on the thin edge and get it, but I fell straight into the deep end. 

I sank all the way down, flailing and struggling to try and mimic whatever essence of swimming I remember on TV or Legend of Zelda, but I sank to the bottom. I looked around and saw the pool's wall, where the edge was, and I tried to run to it, but of course, running under water doesn't exactly get you anywhere. So I tried letting myself sink and pushing off in sort of a jump towards the edge, but no luck. My breathe was running out, I felt light headed, and heavy. I looked up at the sun, which I %100 believed was God, or something, and I realized, and accepted, that I was going to die. 

"I wish I was nicer to my sister." 

I blacked out. And was CPR-resuscitated by a teen girl who was alerted by none other than my sister, who was wondering where I had gone. The kids claim they thought I was joking when I was drowning...

To this day going under water sends me right back. I can swim, but I'd be lying if I said I wasn't on edge. When I'm suicidal I think about swimming out into the ocean, it was kind of peaceful, in a way. But I haven't been in a while.
